A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GOAL study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. V1 Appendix G corresponds to the revised limitations discussion in v2 Section 6.

before.justification: V1 reports original GOAL navigation results on Gibson, MP3D, and HM3D, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and evaluations with multiple seeds.

after.justification: V2 reports original GOAL navigation experiments and supplementary analyses, including the added Flow Matching versus masked-autoencoder comparison in Table 5.

M1.justification: The flow objective, LLM-derived Gaussian priors, scene segmentation, and navigation algorithms are retained. Section 4.3 newly describes prioritizing candidates shared by multiple observed objects as an implementation practice; it does not establish an actual method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gibson and MP3D ObjectNav evaluation and MP3D-to-HM3D transfer, with the same object-category coverage. The added MAE comparison uses these existing tasks and datasets.

E2.justification: V2 Table 5 adds MAE as a comparator in a focused comparison with Flow Matching. V1 already benchmarks the complete SGM system but lacks this algorithm-level comparison. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated GOAL training budget from 20 to 25 epochs, without establishing that retained results were rerun. The new Table 5 comparison uses RedNet instead of GOAL's scene segmentation to control the perception component when comparing MAE and Flow Matching.

E4.justification: V2 adds an analysis testing Flow Matching against MAE under a shared perception setting, separating its contribution from scene segmentation. It removes v1 Figure 1(b)'s qualitative comparison of dependent and Gaussian-source generation. Existing component ablations, sensitivity plots, seed analysis, and navigation examples remain.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2 retains the same five evaluation seeds, reported success rates, aggregate 41.6% ± 0.4%, and use of seed 100 for main results. The added comparison introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 Table 5 adds MAE results and an FM transfer result: on HM3D, MAE versus FM gives SR 32.1 versus 35.9 and DTS 4.85 versus 4.65, while SPL is essentially unchanged at 14.7 versus 14.69. Existing benchmark scores remain numerically unchanged; the FM MP3D row matches v1 Table 3 up to rounding. V1's qualitative conditioning sequence is removed.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, Gaussian-prior definitions, objectives, and Appendix A conditional-flow derivation are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim that conventional conditioning is ill-suited to sparse maps and fails to reconstruct observed regions with an argument about computational overhead. The central contributions and the abstract's and conclusion's navigation and generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies fixed semantic categories as a limitation for novel-category, open-vocabulary settings and interprets the new MAE comparison as supporting transfer generalization. It revises discussion of future flow-training and sampling improvements. The simulated-versus-actual visibility limitation already appears in v1 Appendix G and is relocated.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents prioritization of overlapping candidate sets and explains that the existing conditioning baseline downsamples maps with a convolutional encoder before feeding patches into each DiT block's cross-attention. It also revises the stated epoch count. Code-access information and most appendix implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 removes the ResDiff citation and reframes direct coupling relative to conventional conditioning as greater efficiency without sacrificing performance. The new comparison sharpens positioning against the already-cited MAE/SGM approach; most related work is unchanged apart from reference renumbering.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized introductory and methodological rewrites, moves and revises Appendix G into a main-text discussion section, and adds acknowledgments and author-information updates. It also completes the truncated Appendix C.4 sentence. Most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn without its conditioning-comparison panel, and the MAE-versus-FM table is added. The visibility-mask illustration moves from v1 Figure 9 to v2 Figure 4, with associated table and figure reflow. Other plots and qualitative examples retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new controlled MAE comparison provides more direct evidence for Flow Matching's contribution to transfer performance, and the explicit fixed-category limitation clarifies applicability. These are useful, limited gains: the new comparison adds no uncertainty estimates, existing benchmark scores are unchanged, and removing Figure 1(b) reduces qualitative conditioning evidence. Overall, v2 modestly strengthens the paper's empirical justification and qualification of its claims.
